subject: GCP private offer — drawdown phasing & SKU bucket alignment
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: procurement@acme.ai, it-ops@acme.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, gcp-partner@google.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GCP private offer — drawdown phasing & SKU bucket alignment

Hi team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. I’m attaching an updated commit plan and a SKU mapping export so we can align on a drawdown cadence that matches Acme’s procurement rhythms. Two high-level options we propose: 

- Option A — Smoothing: equal monthly drawdown across 12 months (preferred for predictable burn and to avoid invoice spikes).
- Option B — Front-loaded: 40/30/30 in Q1 for initial scale-up, then even across remaining quarters.

Action items I’m proposing:
- Acme: confirm preferred drawdown option and any PO cadence constraints (monthly/quarterly).
- GCP partner: confirm marketplace SKU mapping and invoice timing for private offers.
- Redwood (Jonas/Marissa): validate SKU bucket pricing and confirm whether we can tag usage to the private-offer IDs for reconciliation.

Attachments: acme_commit_plan_v2.xlsx (proposal with dollar buckets), sku_mapping.csv (raw SKU -> Redwood product mapping).

If useful, I can draft the exact DocuSign update for the private offer once we pick the cadence.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Sales Director | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@acme.ai <procurement@acme.ai>

Subject: Re: GCP private offer — drawdown phasing & SKU bucket alignment

Hi Olga,

Appreciate the options — useful framing. A few constraints from our side: 

- We operate on monthly POs (end of month submission) and cannot do quarterly invoicing without additional approval.
- For accounting, we need invoices that map to the PO month; large single-month charges require pre-approval from finance (we try to avoid >$200k single invoices).
- If we go with the smoothing option, is Redwood/GCP able to emit consumption records and invoices that clearly show the private-offer ID on each billing line? That’s critical for our reconciliation.

Also, a question on refunds/credits: if there’s unused committed consumption at year-end, how are credits handled on the GCP private offer side? Do we get account-level credits or vendor invoices adjusted?

If you can propose a monthly drawdown table aligned to our PO dates, that would speed approval on our side.

Thanks — attaching our standard PO template for reference.

—Jared
Procurement Manager | Acme AI

Jared — quick follow up from our side. Two clarifications while we prepare the monthly table Olga requested: 

1) Billing/Invoice mapping: Jonas, can you confirm whether the marketplace private-offer redemption shows the private-offer ID on the invoice line items (GCP invoice) or whether it appears as a reconciliation line in Google billing export? Procurement needs an explicit invoice-level identifier.

2) Year-end unused commit handling: for private offers there are two common patterns — (a) vendor credit against future invoices (Redwood issues credit memos) or (b) GCP-managed credit applied at the billing account; Jared, which would you prefer for Acme to keep books clean?

We’ll produce a monthly drawdown table that matches Acme’s PO cycle (EOM submission). Olga — we’ll attach that updated spreadsheet to the DocuSign amendment.

Thanks,

Hi Jared / Olga / Marissa — quick update and confirmation from the marketplace side.

- Invoice mapping: GCP billing export will include the private-offer ID as a label on redemption lines, and Redwood can attach the same private-offer identifier to any vendor-side credit memos we issue. For accounting teams, the cleanest approach is to surface the private-offer ID on each invoice line; we confirm we can do that for this private offer.

- Unused commit treatment: Standard approach we recommend for Acme is vendor credit memos issued by Redwood (option a). That gives Acme a clear Redwood credit to apply to future invoices; GCP-side automatic refunds are possible but require monthly reconciliation windows and are slower. We’ll include language for credit memos in the amendment.

- Monthly cadence table: attached is the updated monthly drawdown with PO month alignment and per-month dollar buckets based on Option A smoothing (see sku_mapping.csv). We’ve sized the SKUs so the monthly redemption stays < $175k to avoid the finance threshold Jared mentioned.

Next steps:
1) Acme confirms the smoothing cadence and acceptance of vendor credit memos.
2) Olga to approve DocuSign amendment draft — link below.
3) Once signed, GCP will generate the private-offer redemption schedule and Redwood will issue the first month’s invoice aligned to Acme’s PO.

DocuSign (amendment draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/private-offer
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12897

Attachments: sku_mapping.csv

Thanks,
Jonas
